answer: An agent marketplace for inlet monitoring, prism calibration, and karst mapping requires every bidding identity to lock a $100 bond for 30 days before gaining one vote on job allocation. Voting weight cannot be earned by activity alone, and each additional vote requires a separate bond. An attacker seeking 1,000 votes must therefore immobilize $100,000 for a month; generating new names or keys adds no voting power without additional capital.
